newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq ridicules U.S. statements on power struggle.
newsitem.headline: Iraq ridicules U.S. statements on power struggle.

text.p: An Iraqi government spokesman on Thursday ridiculed U.S. statements alleging a power struggle in Baghdad, saying they were a "distortion and propaganda ploy against Iraq".

"It seems the operating crew of information lies in Washington has resumed its tasks of misleading the public opinion in the United States and renewing fear among Kuwaiti rulers," the spokesman said in a statement published by the official Iraqi News Agency (INA).

"What catches our attention this time is that Samuel Berger, U.S. national security adviser, Mike McCurry, the White House spokesman, (Defence Secretary) William Cohen...and Nicholas Burns, State Department spokesman, are exchanging roles in a distortion and propaganda ploy against Iraq," the spokesman said.
He described the campaign as "a bid to give the kitchen of media lies in Washington some degree of official credibility".

In Washington on Wednesday, McCurry, following suggestions of instability in Iraq reported on Tuesday by a senior U.S. military official, offered a terse but carefully worded assessment of the political situation in Baghdad.
"There are a great deal of complicated internal struggles for power" going on, McCurry said in response to questions on the earlier report.

The senior U.S. military official had said that President Saddam Hussein had put his wife under house arrest and was changing locations more often out of apparent fear for his safety, and that his son Uday, who was shot and wounded in Baghdad on December 12, might lose a leg to gangrene.
The official also said a high source in Baghdad had reported that Saddam was convinced he could recapture Kuwait in a surprise attack.
The Iraqi spokesman said Tuesday's comments had been delivered by new U.S. Defence Secretary Cohen "under the cover of a military official who refused to be identified".
The spokesman added: "World public opinion has become accustomed to such seasonal media bubbles...."
Uday's influential newspaper, Babel, on Thursday published pictures of him in his Baghdad hospital bed receiving Iraqi ministers and other senior officials who wished him good health.
